related_questions.question: What to do if you get fired unfairly?

text_blocks.snippet: If you believe you've been unfairly fired, document everything, collect evidence, understand your rights, and consider seeking legal counsel. Don't sign anything without review, and explore options like filing complaints with HR or government agencies.
snippet_highlighted_words: document everything, collect evidence, understand your rights, and consider seeking legal counsel

list.snippet: Record the details: Write down everything that happened, including dates, times, conversations, and the reasons given for your termination.
Save evidence: Gather performance reviews, emails, and any other documentation that supports your case.
Request a termination letter: Get a written explanation of the reasons for your dismissal.
Review your employment contract: Understand the terms of your employment and any termination clauses.
Identify protected characteristics: Determine if your termination was based on discriminatory reasons (race, gender, religion, etc.).
Consult an attorney: An employment lawyer can advise you on your legal options and guide you through the process.

list.title: File a complaint with HR:
list.snippet: If appropriate, contact your employer's HR department to address your concerns.

list.title: Consider mediation or arbitration:
list.snippet: These alternative dispute resolution methods can help resolve the issue without going to court.

list.title: File a complaint with the EEOC or your state's labor department:
list.snippet: If you believe you were fired due to discrimination or other illegal reasons.

list.title: Consider a lawsuit:
list.snippet: If other options fail, you may need to file a lawsuit against your employer.
Update your resume: Start job searching and focus on your career goals.
Rebuild your confidence: Focus on your strengths and accomplishments.
Don't sign anything without review: Carefully review any agreements or waivers before signing.
